   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2019/904 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 5 June 2019 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment (Text with EEA relevance)», the European Union directive that restricts certain single-use plastic products and fishing gear containing plastic. Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» What the Directive requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive states its objectives as «to prevent and reduce the impact of certain plastic products on the environment, in particular the aquatic environment, and on human health, as well as to promote the transition to a circular economy». Its scope: «This Directive applies to the single-use plastic products listed in the Annex, to products made from oxo-degradable plastic and to fishing gear containing plastic.» A single-use plastic product is defined as «‘single-use plastic product’ means a product that is made wholly or partly from plastic and that is not conceived, designed or placed on the market to accomplish, within its life span, multiple trips or rotations by being returned to a producer for refill or re-used for the same purpose for which it was conceived».

The Directive enters into force on the twentieth day after publication: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .» The header gives the publication date: «12.6.2019 EN Official Journal of the European Union L 155/1»

The Annex ties each product list to an Article. Consumption reduction covers: «PART A Single-use plastic products covered by Article 4 on consumption reduction (1) Cups for beverages, including their covers and lids;» Products Member States must keep off the market include: «PART B Single-use plastic products covered by Article 5 on restrictions on placing on the market (1) Cotton bud sticks, except if they fall within the scope of Council Directive 90/385/EEC ( 1 ) or Council Directive 93/42/EEC ( 2 ) ; (2) Cutlery (forks, knives, spoons, chopsticks); (3) Plates; (4) Straws» Marking covers: «PART D Single-use plastic products covered by Article 7 on marking requirements (1) Sanitary towels (pads), tampons and tampon applicators; (2) Wet wipes, i.e. pre-wetted personal care and domestic wipes; (3) Tobacco products with filters and filters marketed for use in combination with tobacco products; (4) Cups for beverages.» Producer-pays costs for the first group of products cover: «PART E I. Single-use plastic products covered by Article 8(2) on extended producer responsibility (1) Food containers, i.e. receptacles such as boxes, with or without a cover, used to contain food which: (a) is intended for immediate consumption, either on-the-spot or take-away, (b) is typically consumed from the receptacle, and (c) is ready to be consumed without any further preparation, such as cooking, boiling or heating, including food containers used for fast food or other meal ready for immediate consumption, except beverage containers, plates and packets and wrappers containing food; (2) Packets and wrappers made from flexible material containing food that is intended for immediate consumption from the packet or wrapper without any further preparation; (3) Beverage containers with a capacity of up to three litres, i.e. receptacles used to contain liquid such as beverage bottles including their caps and lids and composite beverage packaging including their caps and lids, but not glass or metal beverage containers that have caps and lids made from plastic; (4) Cups for beverages, including their covers and lids; (5) Lightweight plastic carrier bags as defined in point 1c of Article 3 of Directive 94/62/EC.» Collection and recycled-content targets cover: «PART F Single-use plastic products covered by Article 9 on separate collection and by Article 6(5) on product requirements Beverage bottles with a capacity of up to three litres, including their caps and lids,»

*Analytical inference:* because the Directive is addressed to Member States, its duties reach a business through each Member State's national law, and the dates in section 14 are the dates by which Member States apply them. The product lists above rest on the quoted Part headings.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Directive reaches a business only through national law, and only where the business is a producer or a client ships listed products; no 30-day step arises for a freight business that is neither. The steps, each with its trigger:

- At the booking of any shipment into a Member State of a product that may be in Part B («(2) Cutlery (forks, knives, spoons, chopsticks); (3) Plates; (4) Straws»), the commercial lead asks the client to confirm in writing that the product is not in Part B, because «Member States shall prohibit the placing on the market of the single-use plastic products listed in Part B of the Annex and of products made from oxo-degradable plastic.»
- Before the business or a group company first imports Section I of Part E products into a Member State (the list includes «(4) Cups for beverages, including their covers and lids; (5) Lightweight plastic carrier bags as defined in point 1c of Article 3 of Directive 94/62/EC.») and places them on its market, the compliance lead takes to counsel whether it is a producer who must cover the costs: «Member States shall ensure that the producers of the single-use plastic products listed in Section I of Part E of the Annex to this Directive cover the costs pursuant to the extended producer responsibility provisions in Directives 2008/98/EC and 94/62/EC»
- Before a producer first sells such products into a second Member State, the compliance lead asks counsel whether the business is that producer, because the duty to see that an authorised representative is appointed sits with the Member State: «Each Member State shall ensure that a producer established on its territory, which sells single-use plastic products listed in Part E of the Annex and fishing gear containing plastic in another Member State in which it is not established, appoints an authorised representative in that other Member State.»

*Analytical inference:* the three steps rest on the producer definition in section 4 and the Articles quoted above; the Directive states no amount for the producer costs and no EU-wide penalty.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names Member States, producers and authorised representatives. A producer is, in one limb, «any natural or legal person established in a Member State that professionally manufactures, fills, sells or imports, irrespective of the selling technique used, including by means of distance contracts as defined in point (7) of Article 2 of Directive 2011/83/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 21 ) , and places on the market of that Member State single-use plastic products, filled single-use plastic products or fishing gear containing plastic». In a second limb a producer is «any natural or legal person established in one Member State or in a third country that professionally sells in another Member State directly to private households or to users other than private households, by means of distance contracts as defined in point (7) of Article 2 of Directive 2011/83/EU, single-use plastic products, filled single-use plastic products or fishing gear containing plastic». The representative duty sits with the Member State, which must ensure that a producer established on its territory appoints one: «Each Member State shall ensure that a producer established on its territory, which sells single-use plastic products listed in Part E of the Annex and fishing gear containing plastic in another Member State in which it is not established, appoints an authorised representative in that other Member State.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder is not named in the text. A freight business falls within the producer definition only if it professionally manufactures, fills, sells or imports listed products and places them on a Member State's market; moving a client's goods as carrier or forwarder is not one of those activities. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that clears or imports goods on a client's behalf is the person who places them on the market in the Member State concerned.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Commission guidelines named in section 6 are not part of this analysis.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets a series of Commission steps; most dates have passed and nothing held here records whether each was met.

- Standards request: «By 3 October 2019, the Commission shall request the European standardisation organisations to develop harmonised standards relating to the requirement referred to in paragraph 1.»
- Marking specifications: «By 3 July 2020, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act establishing harmonised specifications for the marking referred to in paragraph 1»
- Guidelines on what is a single-use plastic product: «By 3 July 2020, the Commission shall publish guidelines, in consultation with Member States, including examples of what is to be considered a single-use plastic product for the purposes of this Directive, as appropriate.»
- Collection methodology: «By 3 July 2020, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act laying down the methodology for the calculation and verification of the separate collection targets laid down in paragraph 1 of this Article.»
- Consumption reduction methodology: «By 3 January 2021, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act laying down the methodology for the calculation and verification of the ambitious and sustained reduction in the consumption of the single-use plastic products listed in Part A of the Annex.»
- Recycled content calculation rules: «By 1 January 2022, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the rules for the calculation and verification of the targets established in the first subparagraph of this paragraph.»
- Evaluation of the Directive: «The Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Directive by 3 July 2027.»
- Follow-up proposal: «The report shall be accompanied by a legislative proposal, if appropriate. That proposal shall, if appropriate, set binding quantitative consumption reduction targets and set binding collection rates for waste fishing gear.»

*Analytical inference:* the evaluation by 3 July 2027 is the next dated step; the text says its report may carry a legislative proposal setting binding consumption reduction targets, so a business that is a producer should expect the reduction targets to be reviewed after that report. The text does not say whether a proposal will be made.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a food container is inside the Directive is set out in the text: «In order to determine whether a food container is to be considered as a single-use plastic product for the purposes of this Directive, in addition to the criteria listed in the Annex as regards food containers, its tendency to become litter, due to its volume or size, in particular single-serve portions, shall play a decisive role.» The Annex describes a food container as «Food containers, i.e. receptacles such as boxes, with or without a cover, used to contain food which: (a) is intended for immediate consumption, either on-the-spot or take-away, (b) is typically consumed from the receptacle, and (c) is ready to be consumed without any further preparation, such as cooking, boiling or heating, including food containers used for fast food or other meal ready for immediate consumption, except beverage containers, plates and packets and wrappers containing food.» The Commission was to publish examples: «By 3 July 2020, the Commission shall publish guidelines, in consultation with Member States, including examples of what is to be considered a single-use plastic product for the purposes of this Directive, as appropriate.»

*Analytical inference:* a receptacle meeting points (a), (b) and (c) of the Annex description is a food container within the Directive, and one sold in single-serve portions is more likely to be treated as single-use because size and litter tendency are decisive. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given container on a client's route meets points (a), (b) and (c) and the litter test.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. «This Directive applies to the single-use plastic products listed in the Annex, to products made from oxo-degradable plastic and to fishing gear containing plastic.»

Consumption reduction. «Those measures shall achieve a measurable quantitative reduction in the consumption of the single-use plastic products listed in Part A of the Annex on the territory of the Member State by 2026 compared to 2022.»

Market restriction. «Member States shall prohibit the placing on the market of the single-use plastic products listed in Part B of the Annex and of products made from oxo-degradable plastic.»

Product requirements. «Member States shall ensure that single-use plastic products listed in Part C of the Annex that have caps and lids made of plastic may be placed on the market only if the caps and lids remain attached to the containers during the products’ intended use stage.» Recycled content: «(a) from 2025, beverage bottles listed in Part F of the Annex which are manufactured from polyethylene terephthalate as the major component (‘PET bottles’) contain at least 25 % recycled plastic, calculated as an average for all PET bottles placed on the market on the territory of that Member State; and (b) from 2030, beverage bottles listed in Part F of the Annex contain at least 30 % recycled plastic, calculated as an average for all such beverage bottles placed on the market on the territory of that Member State.»

Marking. «Member States shall ensure that each single-use plastic product listed in Part D of the Annex placed on the market bears a conspicuous, clearly legible and indelible marking on its packaging or on the product itself informing consumers of the following:»

Extended producer responsibility. «Member States shall ensure that extended producer responsibility schemes are established for all single-use plastic products listed in Part E of the Annex which are placed on the market of the Member State, in accordance with Articles 8 and 8a of Directive 2008/98/EC.» Producers of the products in Section I of Part E bear stated costs: «Member States shall ensure that the producers of the single-use plastic products listed in Section I of Part E of the Annex to this Directive cover the costs pursuant to the extended producer responsibility provisions in Directives 2008/98/EC and 94/62/EC and, insofar as not already included, cover the following costs: (a) the costs of the awareness raising measures referred to in Article 10 of this Directive regarding those products; (b) the costs of waste collection for those products that are discarded in public collection systems, including the infrastructure and its operation, and the subsequent transport and treatment of that waste; and (c) the costs of cleaning up litter resulting from those products and the subsequent transport and treatment of that litter.»

Separate collection. Member States must collect: «(a) by 2025, of an amount of waste single-use plastic products listed in Part F of the Annex equal to 77 % of such single-use plastic products placed on the market in a given year by weight; (b) by 2029, of an amount of waste single-use plastic products listed in Part F of the Annex equal to 90 % of such single-use plastic products placed on the market in a given year by weight.»

Penalties. «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of national provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.»

Transposition. «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 3 July 2021.» Some measures apply on later dates: «However, the Member States shall apply the measures necessary to comply with: — Article 5 from 3 July 2021, — Article 6(1) from 3 July 2024, — Article 7(1) from 3 July 2021, — Article 8 by 31 December 2024 but, in relation to extended producer responsibility schemes established before 4 July 2018 and in relation to single-use plastic products listed in Section III of Part E of the Annex, by 5 January 2023.» National agreements may replace some measures: «Member States may transpose the provisions set out in Articles 4(1) and 8(1) and (8), except as regards single-use plastic products listed in Section III of Part E of the Annex, by means of agreements between the competent authorities and the economic sectors concerned.»

*Analytical inference:* each requirement falls on Member States, which pass the duty to producers through national law; the producer-pays costs are stated as costs producers cover, and the text states no pass-through of those costs to a customer, so any effect on freight rates is not stated. The recycled content and collection percentages are national averages and national rates, not a rule for each shipment. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business is a producer in a given Member State and which national measure transposes each Article there.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

Each Part of the Annex ties a product list to an Article: Part B to the market ban («PART B Single-use plastic products covered by Article 5 on restrictions on placing on the market»), Part C to product requirements («PART C Single-use plastic products covered by Article 6(1) to (4) on product requirements»), Part D to marking («PART D Single-use plastic products covered by Article 7 on marking requirements»), Part E to producer-pays costs («PART E I. Single-use plastic products covered by Article 8(2) on extended producer responsibility») and Part F to collection and recycled content («PART F Single-use plastic products covered by Article 9 on separate collection and by Article 6(5) on product requirements»).

*Analytical inference:* a product therefore has a different status by Part: banned, attached caps, marked, producer-paid or counted toward collection. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which Part a client's specific product falls in and which national measure applies to it.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Representation. «Each Member State shall allow the producers established in another Member State and placing products on its market to appoint a legal or natural person established on its territory as an authorised representative for the purposes of fulfilling the obligations of a producer related to extended producer responsibility schemes on its territory.» «The authorised representative shall be the person responsible for fulfilling the obligations of that producer pursuant to this Directive on the territory of that other Member State.»

Reporting by Member States. «Member States shall, for each calendar year, report to the Commission the following: (a) data on single-use plastic products listed in Part A of the Annex that have been placed on the market of the Member State each year, to demonstrate the consumption reduction in accordance with Article 4(1);» «The first reporting period shall be the calendar year 2022, with the exception of points (e) and (f) of the first subparagraph for which the first reporting period shall be the calendar year 2023.»

*Analytical inference:* the reporting duty falls on Member States, not on a producer. The text does not state a producer register or a registration deadline for producers. *Legal Confirmation Required:* what a producer must register in the Member State where it sells, which the national law decides.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: no system change is due for a freight business that is not a producer. When a business is found to be a producer (the section 3 check), its compliance lead checks at each new product on a lane which Part of the Annex lists it (section 9) before the next shipment is booked. Costs: «The costs to be covered referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 shall not exceed the costs that are necessary to provide the services referred to therein in a cost-efficient way and shall be established in a transparent way between the actors concerned.» Marking: «The harmonised marking specifications shall be established by the Commission in accordance with paragraph 2.» Food rules: «The measures that Member States take to transpose and implement Articles 4 to 9 of this Directive shall comply with Union food law to ensure that food hygiene and food safety are not compromised.»

*Analytical inference:* the per-product check rests on the Part headings quoted in section 9, which decide whether a product is banned, marked or producer-paid.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Two edge cases are stated. Caps: «For the purposes of this Article, metal caps or lids with plastic seals shall not be considered to be made of plastic.» Agreements: «Member States may transpose the provisions set out in Articles 4(1) and 8(1) and (8), except as regards single-use plastic products listed in Section III of Part E of the Annex, by means of agreements between the competent authorities and the economic sectors concerned.»

*Analytical inference:* a metal cap with a plastic seal is outside the attached cap rule, and some Member States may meet two Articles through sector agreements instead of a law. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a Member State has used such an agreement for products on a client's lane.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1106 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 11 April 2024 amending Regulations (EU) No 1227/2011 and (EU) 2019/942 as regards improving the Union’s protection against market manipulation on the wholesale energy market (Text with EEA relevance)», the European Union act that amends the rules on trading in wholesale electricity, gas and liquefied natural gas. Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation changes two earlier European Union acts. It states its aim as «to ensure further transparency and increase monitoring capacities, thereby contributing to the stabilisation of energy prices and consumer protection». Its reach: «This Regulation applies to trading in wholesale energy products.» The products are defined by contract type, for example «contracts for the supply of electricity or natural gas, including LNG, where delivery is in the Union». The persons bound are market participants: «“market participant” means any person, including transmission system operators, distribution system operators, storage system operators and LNG system operators, who enters into transactions, including the placing of orders to trade, in one or more wholesale energy markets». The energy regulators' agency, called the Agency in the text, is described as «the European Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (the ‘Agency’)».

The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after publication, and two parts apply on later dates: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . 2. By way of derogation from paragraph 1, the following dates of application shall apply: (a) Article 1, points (6) and (13), as regards Article 4a (1) to (7) and Article 9a (1) to (5) of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011, shall apply from the date on which the delegated acts adopted pursuant to those points enter into force; (b) Article 1, point (10), as regards Articles 7a to 7e of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011, shall apply from 1 January 2025; (c) Article 1, point (18), as regards Article 15(2) of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011, shall apply from 8 November 2024.» The header gives the publication date: «L series 2024/1106 17.4.2024 REGULATION (EU) 2024/1106»

*Analytical inference:* counting twenty days from the publication date in the header, 17.4.2024, gives 7 May 2024, the date from which the text starts a five-year delegation to the Commission (section 6). The Regulation reaches a business only if it is a market participant as defined above; the text names no freight forwarder, carrier or shipper, so the duties below turn on whether a business enters transactions in electricity, gas or LNG supply contracts or their derivatives.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this Regulation falls on a business that does not trade electricity, gas or LNG supply contracts or derivatives, so no action is due within 30 days for a freight business in that position. The steps for a business that may be in scope are:

- At the next renewal of any energy supply contract, and before any new one or any derivative is signed, a contracts lead lists every electricity and natural gas supply contract the business holds, and every derivative on them, and records whether the business enters transactions on a wholesale energy market, which is the test for a market participant.
- If any group company does enter such transactions, the compliance lead takes the disclosure, reporting and registration duties in sections 8 and 10 to counsel before the next trade, because the fines in section 8 attach to the market participant.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the market participant definition in section 2. The text states no duty of any kind for a business that only uses energy.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names market participants, organised marketplaces, persons professionally arranging or executing transactions, the Agency and national regulatory authorities. A person professionally arranging or executing transactions is defined as «“person professionally arranging or executing transactions” means a person professionally engaged in the reception and transmission of orders for, or in the execution of transactions in, wholesale energy products». An organised marketplace is defined as «“organised marketplace” or “OMP” means an energy exchange, an energy broker, an energy capacity platform or any other system or facility in which multiple third-party buying or selling interests in wholesale energy products interact in a manner that may result in a transaction». Those persons carry a reporting duty: «Any person professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products who reasonably suspects that an order to trade or a transaction, including any cancellation or modification thereof, whether placed on or outside an OMP, could breach Article 3, 4 or 5, shall notify the Agency and the relevant national regulatory authority without further delay and in any event no later than four weeks from the day on which that person becomes aware of the suspicious event.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder is not named in any of these roles. A freight business would take the arranging or executing role only if it receives and transmits orders for, or executes, transactions in wholesale energy products, which is not a freight activity. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any group company is a market participant or a person professionally arranging or executing transactions, and in which Member State it would register.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets dated steps for the Agency, the Commission and Member States. Most dates have passed and nothing held here records whether each was met.

- Agency platform: «By 8 May 2025, the Agency shall develop and operate a platform serving as a sector-specific electronic access point for inside information disclosed pursuant to paragraph 1.»
- Delegated act on inside information platforms: «By 8 May 2025, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 20 to supplement this Regulation by specifying: (a) the means by which an IIP is to fulfil the obligation to make public the inside information laid down in paragraph 3 of this Article;»
- Implementing acts on order book reporting: «By 8 May 2025, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the further details regarding the operation of this paragraph, including the specific arrangements for ensuring effective data reporting.»
- Yearly Agency report on suspicious-transaction arrangements: «By 8 May 2025 and every year thereafter, the Agency shall, in cooperation with national regulatory authorities, issue and make public a report with aggregated information»
- Report on criminal penalties: «By 1 June 2025 the Commission shall assess the effectiveness of introducing criminal penalties by Member States for intentional and serious cases of market abuse on the Union wholesale energy markets and shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council.»
- Member State notification of penalty provisions, where a court imposes fines: «Those Member States shall notify the Commission of the provisions of their laws which they adopt pursuant to this paragraph by 8 May 2026»
- Report on consistency of penalties: «By 8 May 2027 and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council, assessing whether penalties for breaches of this Regulation are provided for and applied consistently across the Member States.»
- Review of the Regulation: «By 1 June 2027, and every five years thereafter, the Commission shall, after consulting relevant stakeholders, assess the application of this Regulation, in particular as regards its impact on market behaviour, market participants, liquidity, reporting requirements, including on LNG market data, and the level of administrative burden for market participants»
- Delegation period for the new delegated acts: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 4a(8), Article 6(1), point (c), and Article 9a(6) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 7 May 2024.»
- Earlier delegation period: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 6(1), points (a) and (b), shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 28 December 2011.»

*Analytical inference:* the review due by 1 June 2027 assesses the administrative burden on market participants and reporting requirements, so the reporting duties in section 10 are the part most open to change; a business that is a market participant should expect to revisit its reporting set-up after that report, and a business that is not one is unaffected. The text states no content for the report beyond its listed subjects.

What each date changes for a reader: from 1 January 2025 the LNG articles apply, so a person who engages in LNG trading («“LNG market participant” means any natural or legal person, irrespective of that person’s place of incorporation or domicile, who engages in LNG trading») has had to supply daily data: «LNG market participants shall submit daily to the Agency the LNG market data, free of charge,» *Analytical inference:* that applies to such a person only, and rests on the two quoted definitions and duties. On 8 May 2026, nothing changes for a market participant: the date is when Member States notify the Commission of their national court-fine provisions, and the fines a business faces stay those set in national law. On 8 May 2027, nothing changes for a business either: the Commission reports on whether penalties are applied consistently, and the report itself changes nothing for a business.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. «This Regulation applies to trading in wholesale energy products.»

Market abuse. The Regulation defines market manipulation to include «entering into any transaction, or issuing, modifying or withdrawing any order to trade or engaging in any other behaviour relating to wholesale energy products which: (i) gives, or is likely to give, false or misleading signals as to the supply of, demand for, or price of wholesale energy products». It also treats cancelling or amending an order as insider trading in one case: «The use of inside information by cancelling or amending an order, or any other trading action concerning a wholesale energy product to which the information relates, where the order was placed before the person concerned possessed the inside information, shall also be considered to be insider trading.»

Disclosure. «Market participants shall disclose the inside information through IIPs.»

Algorithmic trading. «A market participant that engages in algorithmic trading shall have in place effective systems and risk controls suitable to the business it operates to ensure that its trading systems are resilient and have sufficient capacity»
